author: Linnaeus, 1758

points.en: buff breast and flanks heavily marked with black streaks and spots

art.subject: Fieldfare (Turdus pilaris), adult in winter (sexes similar): head and nape blue-grey with a faint whitish supercilium and dark lores; mantle and scapulars rich chestnut-brown; rump pale blue-grey; wings brown; tail blackish; throat and breast washed golden-buff and heavily marked with black arrowhead spots and streaks; flanks white with dense black chevrons; belly white; bill yellow with a dark tip; dark eye; dark brown legs.
art.pose: perched on a bare branch with berries, side view
art.scene: orchard edge and berry shrubs in Korea in winter, light snow on the ground; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view perched upright on a bare branch with berries: large robust thrush, blue-grey head and nape, yellow bill, chestnut-brown back, pale grey rump, buff breast and flanks heavily marked with black streaks and spots, whitish belly, long black tail

adult, in flight seen squarely from above: head, body and tail in one line, wings spread straight out to the sides to their full span, blue-grey head, chestnut-brown back, pale grey rump contrasting with the long black tail, brownish wings

adult, in flight seen squarely from below: wings spread straight out to the sides to their full span, white underwing coverts, buff breast with black spots, whitish belly, long black tail, yellow bill, feet tucked against the body
art.build: A large, robust thrush, larger than a Dusky Thrush, with an upright stance and a long tail. Rounded head. Bill straight and stout, slightly shorter than the head. Legs medium, dark brown. Tail long, square, blackish, contrasting with the grey rump in flight. In flight the underwing coverts are white. Usually in flocks feeding on berries or open fields.
avoid: Do not paint a brown head or rump; both are grey, contrasting with the chestnut back.
Do not paint a bold white supercilium (Redwing); it is faint.
Do not paint evenly spaced round spots on white (Mistle Thrush); the breast is golden-buff with arrowhead spots.
Do not give it a brown tail; it is blackish.
